content.overview: Without prejudice to section 391, if a foreign company contravenes Chapter XXII, the company is punishable with fine not less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to three lakh rupees, and for a continuing contravention with an additional fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees for every day after the first during which the contravention continues. Every officer of the foreign company who is in default is punishable with fine not less than twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees. Imprisonment was removed by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2020.
content.glance: Foreign company: fine ₹1 lakh–₹3 lakh (+ up to ₹50,000/day continuing); officer in default: fine ₹25,000–₹5 lakh; no imprisonment after 2020 Amendment.
content.study: Section 392 is the Chapter XXII penalty provision. It operates without prejudice to section 391. The 2020 Amendment removed the imprisonment component for officers; current text is fine-based.

sections.heading: Company fine
sections.body: ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh; continuing: up to ₹50,000 per day after the first.

examples.title: Application of Section 392
examples.body: Facts satisfying the elements in the statutory text of Section 392 produce the consequence described in that section.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage Section 392?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare facts with the statutory elements in Section 392.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 392
distinctions.body: Section 392 applies only within its statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Officers still face imprisonment under section 392.
misconceptions.correction: The 2020 Amendment removed imprisonment; liability is fine-based.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 392 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify Chapter XXII contravention by a foreign company. II. Apply company and officer fines. III. Note continuing daily fine. IV. Conclude (no imprisonment).

enhancement.definition: Section 392 imposes fine-based punishment on foreign companies and officers in default for Chapter XXII contraventions.
